![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/9d0b7f238afe0f6cb82bb8670b9589aa10490b6e776e7f4a991a561aa0ad2245.png)

Consider the region bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt{4-x}$ and the horizontal line $y=1$ from $x=0$ to $x=3,$ as shown in the picture. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated ${360}^{∘}$about the line $y=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=3$ along the $x$-axis.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/73fc1e2cad0969a629e2c2c4a55ce8ac66c16b67fe2984e8b75dc6aa3a5eeace.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=1,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=\sqrt{4-x}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}{[\,(\sqrt{4-x})-(1)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}((4-x)-2\sqrt{4-x}+1)\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}(5-x-2\sqrt{4-x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi (5{\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{3}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{3}\sqrt{4-x}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\pi (5x{|}_{0}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{3}+\frac{4}{3}(4-x)^{3/2}{|}_{0}^{3}) \\  & =\pi ((15-0)-(\frac{9}{2}-0)+\frac{4}{3}(1-8)) \\  & =\pi (15-\frac{9}{2}-\frac{28}{3}) \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
